chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Umar ibn Yazid from Burayd al-Ajli said:

I asked him about a man who manumitted his slave by contract (mukatabah) for one thousand dirhams, and did not stipulate upon him at the time of contract that if he were unable to complete the payment, he would return to slavery. And that the mukatab paid his master five hundred dirhams, then the mukatab died leaving a mature son. He said: 'Half of whatever the mukatab left is for his master who contracted with him, and the remaining half is for the son of the mukatab, because the mukatab died and half of him is free and half is a slave to the one who contracted with him. So the son of the mukatab is like the state of his father: half free and half slave to the one who contracted with his father. If he pays to the one who contracted with his father what remained on his father, then he becomes free, and there is no claim of anyone from the people upon him.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This is the report, and that which we presented at the beginning of the chapter from Muhammad ibn Qays is that upon which I act and by which I give fatwa, and it is that the master inherits from the estate of the mukatab if it was not stipulated upon him to the extent of what remained of his slavery, and the remainder is for his son, and it is incumbent upon him to pay to the master of his father what remained on his father so that he becomes free and deserves what remains of the wealth. And this does not contradict the report we presented from Abdullah ibn Sinan and Malik ibn Atiyyah that if he pays what remained on his father, then what remains is for him, because in these reports it is not [stated] that if he pays what remained on his father from the principal wealth or from what he acquires. And if we assume that, we interpret it as: if he pays what remained on his father from what is specific to him, then after that if something remains, it is for him. And upon this, all the reports are reconciled.

key_terms.رَدٌّ فِي الرِّقِّ: Returning to slavery (if unable to pay)
key_terms.مكاتبة: The contract of manumission by payment
key_terms.مُكَاتَب: A slave who has entered into a contract with his master to pay a specific sum for his manumission
key_terms.نِصْفُهُ حُرٌّ وَ نِصْفُهُ عَبْدٌ: Half free and half slave (a state of partial manumission)

ai.seo_question: How is the estate of a mukatab distributed between the master and his son upon death?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, detailing the partial manumission status of a mukatab who dies with an unpaid debt, resulting in a half-slave, half-free estate division between the master and the son. Al-Tusi highlights a scholarly nuance by reconciling this with other reports, clarifying that the son's payment of the residual debt secures his full freedom and exclusive claim to the remaining estate, a principle central to Shia jurisprudence on mukatab inheritance.
